rules.title: Compliance policies protect Windows devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: At least one Intune compliance policy for Windows (windows10CompliancePolicy / windows11CompliancePolicy) must exist and be assigned. Without it, noncompliant Windows endpoints can reach corporate resources and Conditional Access cannot rely on device health.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy (Windows 10 and later), configure BitLocker, password, firewall and OS version requirements, then assign it to device or user groups.

links.text: Create and assign Intune compliance policies

rules.title: Compliance policies protect macOS devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: At least one Intune compliance policy for macOS must exist and be assigned so that macOS devices are evaluated for health before accessing corporate data.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy (macOS), define FileVault, firewall, Gatekeeper and OS requirements, then assign it.

links.text: Create and assign Intune compliance policies

rules.title: Compliance policies protect iOS/iPadOS devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: At least one Intune compliance policy for iOS/iPadOS must exist and be assigned so that Apple mobile devices are evaluated for jailbreak status, passcode and OS version.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy (iOS/iPadOS), set passcode, jailbreak and OS version requirements, then assign it.

links.text: Create and assign Intune compliance policies

rules.title: Compliance policies protect fully managed and corporate-owned Android devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No Android Enterprise fully managed compliance policy exists
rules.description: At least one compliance policy for Android Enterprise fully managed / corporate-owned devices must exist and be assigned.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy > Android Enterprise > Fully managed, dedicated, and corporate-owned work profile, then assign it.

links.text: Create and assign Intune compliance policies

rules.title: Compliance policies protect personally owned Android devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No Android work profile compliance policy exists
rules.description: At least one compliance policy for Android Enterprise personally-owned work profile devices must exist and be assigned.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Compliance > Create policy > Android Enterprise > Personally-owned work profile, then assign it.

links.text: Create and assign Intune compliance policies

rules.title: Data on iOS/iPadOS is protected by app protection policies
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No iOS app protection policy exists
rules.description: At least one assigned Intune app protection policy for iOS/iPadOS must exist to stop corporate data leaking into unmanaged apps.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Apps > App protection policies > Create > iOS/iPadOS, configure data transfer, encryption and access requirements, then assign it.

rules.title: Data on Android is protected by app protection policies
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No Android app protection policy exists
rules.description: At least one assigned Intune app protection policy for Android must exist to stop corporate data leaking into unmanaged apps.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Apps > App protection policies > Create > Android, configure data transfer, encryption and access requirements, then assign it.

rules.title: Windows Update policies are enforced to reduce risk from unpatched vulnerabilities
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: At least one assigned Windows Update for Business update ring (windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration) must exist so that Windows devices receive security patches on schedule.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Windows > Windows updates > Update rings > Create profile, then assign it.

links.text: Manage Windows software updates in Intune

rules.title: Device enrollment notifications are enforced to ensure user awareness and secure onboarding
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: An assigned enrollment notification policy should exist so users learn when a device is enrolled, helping detect unauthorised enrolment.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Enrollment > Enrollment notifications > Create notification, then assign it.

rules.title: Security baselines are applied to Windows devices to strengthen security posture
rules.name: displayName
rules.description: At least one assigned Intune security baseline profile must exist to standardise hardened Windows settings.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Endpoint security > Security baselines > pick a baseline > Create profile, then assign it.

rules.title: Endpoint Analytics is enabled to help identify risks on Windows devices
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No endpoint analytics (health monitoring) profile exists
rules.description: An assigned Windows health monitoring profile (windowsHealthMonitoringConfiguration) must exist to enable endpoint analytics data collection.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Reports > Endpoint analytics > Settings > Intune data collection policy, and assign it to Windows devices.

rules.title: Device cleanup rules maintain tenant hygiene by hiding inactive devices
rules.name: id
rules.description: At least one Intune device cleanup rule should exist so stale devices are hidden and the device inventory stays accurate.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Organize devices > Device cleanup rules > configure the number of days before inactive devices are removed.

rules.title: Defender for Endpoint automatic enrollment is enforced to reduce risk from unmanaged Android threats
rules.name: id
rules.empty_message: Defender for Endpoint connector is not configured
rules.description: The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector must be enabled in Intune with Android device connection turned on, so Android devices are automatically onboarded for mobile threat defence.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Endpoint security > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint > turn on Connect Android devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

links.text: Integrate Defender for Endpoint with Intune

rules.title: Secure Wi-Fi profiles protect iOS devices from unauthorized network access
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No enterprise Wi-Fi profile for iOS/iPadOS exists
rules.description: At least one assigned iOS/iPadOS Wi-Fi profile using enterprise (certificate/802.1X) authentication must exist, instead of pre-shared keys.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Configuration > Create > iOS/iPadOS > Wi-Fi, choose an Enterprise security type, then assign it.

rules.title: Secure Wi-Fi profiles protect Android devices from unauthorized network access
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No enterprise Wi-Fi profile for Android Enterprise exists
rules.description: At least one assigned Android Enterprise Wi-Fi profile using enterprise (certificate/802.1X) authentication must exist, instead of pre-shared keys.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Configuration > Create > Android Enterprise > Wi-Fi, choose an Enterprise security type, then assign it.

rules.title: Secure Wi-Fi profiles protect macOS devices from unauthorized network access
rules.name: displayName
rules.empty_message: No enterprise Wi-Fi profile for macOS exists
rules.description: At least one assigned macOS Wi-Fi profile using enterprise (certificate/802.1X) authentication must exist, instead of pre-shared keys.
rules.remediation: Intune admin center > Devices > Configuration > Create > macOS > Wi-Fi, choose an Enterprise security type, then assign it.
